t:
(a) In General.—Whenever the transfer of ownership of a Coast Guard vessel or aircraft to an eligible entity for use for educational, cultural, historical, charitable, recreational, or other public purposes is authorized by law or declared excess by the Commandant, the Coast Guard shall transfer the vessel or aircraft to the General Services Administration for conveyance to the eligible entity. 
    (b) Conditions of Conveyance.—The General Services Administration may not convey a vessel or aircraft to an eligible entity as authorized by law unless the eligible entity agrees—
        (1) to provide the documentation needed by the General Services Administration to process a request for aircraft or vessels under section 102.37.225 of title 41, Code of Federal Regulations; 
        (2) to comply with the special terms, conditions, and restrictions imposed on aircraft and vessels under section 102.37.460 of such title; 
        (3) to make the vessel available to the United States Government if it is needed for use by the Commandant of the Coast Guard in time of war or a national emergency; and 
        (4) to hold the United States Government harmless for any claims arising from exposure to hazardous materials, including asbestos and polychlorinated biphenyls, that occurs after conveyance of the vessel, except for claims arising from use of the vessel by the United States Government under paragraph (3).  
    (c) Other Obligations Unaffected.—Nothing in this section amends or affects any obligation of the Coast Guard or any other person under the Toxic Substances Control Act (15 U.S.C. 2601 et seq.) or any other law regarding use or disposal of hazardous materials including asbestos and polychlorinated biphenyls. 
    (d) Eligible Entity Defined.—In this section, the term “eligible entity” means a State or local government, nonprofit corporation, educational agency, community development organization, or other entity that agrees to comply with the conditions established under this section.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that states, local governments and nonprofits are involved because they are "eligible entities" that must agree to conditions. But they are only recipients of surplus property accepting conveyance terms, which is like an application for a benefit, not consultation on a federal decision. The only coordination is the transfer from the Coast Guard to the General Services Administration, which stays inside the federal government. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue.
fable.s: The General Services Administration may not convey a vessel or aircraft to an eligible entity as authorized by law unless the eligible entity agrees

qwen_block.w: This section outlines the conditions an outside entity must agree to in order to receive a government asset (a vessel or aircraft). This is effectively an application or acceptance process for a grant or transfer of property, not a mechanism for the outside entity to participate in the federal decision-making process. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants. The outside entity does not consult with the government on policy or decision-making; rather, they must accept pre-determined terms to receive the asset.
qwen_block.s: The General Services Administration may not convey a vessel or aircraft to an eligible entity as authorized by law unless the eligible entity agrees— (1) to provide the documentation needed by the General Services Administration to process a request for aircraft or vessels under section 102.37.225 of title 41, Code of Federal Regulations; (2) to comply with the special terms, conditions, and restrictions imposed on aircraft and vessels under section 102.37.460 of such title; (3) to make the vessel available to the United States Government if it is needed for use by the Commandant of the Coast Guard in time of war or a national emergency; and (4) to hold the United States Government harmless for any claims arising from exposure to hazardous materials, including asbestos and polychlorinated biphenyls, that occurs after conveyance of the vessel, except for claims arising from use of the vessel by the United States Government under paragraph (3).

opus.w: The section sets conditions under which non-federal entities can receive surplus Coast Guard vessels or aircraft. That is a transfer of property, like applying for a benefit, so it is excluded as participation. The CFR provisions are cited only as existing requirements to comply with; the section does not authorize new rulemaking. No outside party is consulted on a federal decision, given a hearing or comment period, or granted a right to sue.
opus.s: The General Services Administration may not convey a vessel or aircraft to an eligible entity as authorized by law unless the eligible entity agrees—
opus.b:
**Tempting reading:** Outside parties are involved here. States, local governments, nonprofits and other "eligible entities" deal with GSA, and the section refers to federal regulations (41 CFR 102.37.225 and 102.37.460), which could look like rulemaking.

**Why it fails:** These entities are receiving property. They ask for a vessel or aircraft and agree to the conditions attached to it, which is like applying for a benefit. They are not consulted on any federal decision. The regulations cited already exist. The section only says entities must follow them, and it gives no new authority to issue regulations. There is also no hearing, comment period, advisory body, consultation requirement or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section describes the conditions under which the federal government transfers assets to outside entities. The outside entities are applicants/recipients of a benefit (the vessel/aircraft), and their agreement to terms is part of the application/acceptance process, not a consultation or coordination on a federal decision. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants from being considered participation.
qwen_chat.s: The General Services Administration may not convey a vessel or aircraft to an eligible entity as authorized by law unless the eligible entity agrees— (1) to provide the documentation needed by the General Services Administration to process a request for aircraft or vessels under section 102.37.225 of title 41, Code of Federal Regulations; (2) to comply with the special terms, conditions, and restrictions imposed on aircraft and vessels under section 102.37.460 of such title; (3) to make the vessel available to the United States Government if it is needed for use by the Commandant of the Coast Guard in time of war or a national emergency; and (4) to hold the United States Government harmless for any claims arising from exposure to hazardous materials...
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because "eligible entities" (states, nonprofits, etc.) must agree to conditions before receiving a vessel, this constitutes participation. However, the definition explicitly states that "applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses... applying for something is not participating in the decision." Here, the outside entity is applying for/receiving a government asset (a benefit/transfer), and the conditions are prerequisites for that transfer, not a mechanism for the outside entity to consult on or influence a federal policy decision. The federal government (Coast Guard/GSA) makes the decision to transfer; the outside entity merely accepts terms.
